agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards establishes sackcloth as mourning clothing. Even with the shaved heads and clipped beards in the question, a baker working only from those cards cannot derive sackcloth rather than leather or silk; the blank depends on already knowing or luckily guessing the unseen wording.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

agent.problem: Card 6 says only that what is coming has wings. Eagle, raven and stork all fit that setup, and nothing in the earlier cards makes eagle inferable, so this fill-in-the-blank asks the baker to guess the next word of a line they have not seen.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

agent.problem: "In that day" points back to card 8 for the capture of Kirioth and the seizure of the strongholds, but that story card is no longer on screen. The question needs to carry those events itself so the baker has the context for the warriors' reaction.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
